story: Alaska moved 3,048 registered voters to inactive status after a DMV citizenship list comparison, and legislators demanded restoration weeks before the August 18 primary

claims.claim: The Alaska Division of Elections checks its voter list against Division of Motor Vehicles data every three months, and the check usually returns about 200 names.
claims.verbatim: Every three months, she said, the Elections Division checks its voter list against the Division of Motor Vehicles data, looking for people who may have said they were not citizens when they got their drivers licenses. Usually, they get about 200 names.
claims.notes: The baseline figure. Beecher's testimony relayed by a reporter, not an agency document. Nothing on the page describes the match logic beyond comparing the two lists.

claims.claim: Elections Director Carol Beecher said the division sent a letter to about 3,500 Alaskans after the most recent list comparison.
claims.verbatim: She said her agency sent a letter to about 3,500 Alaskans.
claims.notes: Hedged as 'about 3,500' in the source. Letters SENT is a different quantity from the 3,048 moved to inactive. Do not conflate. Do not build a slide on this figure alone.

claims.claim: A Division of Elections spokesman gave the specific figure of 3,048.
claims.verbatim: (A spokesman for the division later provided a specific number: 3,048)
claims.notes: The agency's own number reported secondhand. Corroborated by C04 a week later.

claims.claim: The Division of Elections moved 3,048 voters to the inactive list over questions about their citizenship.
claims.verbatim: The Division of Elections revealed this month that it moved 3,048 voters to the "inactive" list due to questions about their citizenship.
claims.notes: Same newsroom as C03, so corroboration rather than an independent second source. The sources say INACTIVE, never 'removed' or 'purged'. The deck must use inactive.

claims.claim: Carol Beecher said some of the data behind the flags is probably very old data from people who never told DMV they had naturalized.
claims.verbatim: So we understand that some of this is probably very old data, where the individuals did not contact DMV, have not updated that they are a naturalized citizen,
claims.notes: Verbatim, confirmed on targeted re-fetch. The load-bearing quote. 'Probably' is Beecher's own hedge and must not be hardened.

claims.claim: Beecher acknowledged the old-data problem to legislators at a hearing in Anchorage on Wednesday, July 22, 2026.
claims.verbatim: State Director of Elections Carol Beecher acknowledged to legislators at a hearing in Anchorage Wednesday that the allegations may be based on "very old data."
claims.notes: The page says 'Wednesday'; the story published Thursday 2026-07-23, so Wednesday is 2026-07-22 by inference. No fetched page names the committee, so the deck must not name one.

claims.claim: Beecher said people who got the letter can check a box to indicate they are citizens, or call or email the division.
claims.verbatim: Beecher said people who got the letter can just check a box to indicate they are citizens, or call or email the division.
claims.notes: The burden-shift beat. No fetched page says documentary proof of naturalization is required, so the deck must not claim that.

claims.claim: Beecher said voters who do not respond to the letter will remain on the inactive list.
claims.verbatim: She said voters who don't respond to the letter will remain on the inactive list.
claims.notes: Silence defaults to inactive. The single strongest sentence for the deck's thesis about who carries the burden after an automated flag.

claims.claim: Beecher said affected voters can still vote a questioned ballot, attesting that they are a citizen and a valid voter.
claims.verbatim: But she said they can still vote a questioned ballot, attesting that they are a citizen and a valid voter.
claims.notes: Fairness beat. Inactive status does not by itself stop someone voting. No source says how these questioned ballots will be adjudicated.

claims.claim: Rep. Andrew Gray told Beecher that the people contacting his office are actual citizens receiving the notice.
claims.verbatim: "The reason why I think the folks are reaching out to our office is because these are actual citizens who are receiving this notice," Gray told her.
claims.notes: Attribute as Rep. Andrew Gray with no party label; the retrieved sentence did not carry one.

claims.claim: Rep. Kevin McCabe defended the division, saying keeping the voter rolls clean and correct is what it is supposed to do.
claims.verbatim: "This is actually their job," he said. "This is what they do, is make sure the voter rolls are clean and correct."
claims.notes: REQUIRED for fairness. This is the counterweight that keeps the deck from being one sided. Attribute as Rep. Kevin McCabe with no party label.

claims.claim: A bipartisan group of 23 legislators wrote to Beecher asking that all names be put back on the active voters list unless ineligibility has been established.
claims.verbatim: A bipartisan group of 23 legislators wrote a letter Tuesday, asking Elections Director Carol Beecher to put all names back on the active voters list unless their ineligibility to vote has been established.
claims.notes: CONFLICTS WITH C13 (20 per Alaska's News Source). The letter itself was unreachable. Any on-slide number must be attributed to the outlet or given as a range.

claims.claim: Alaska's News Source reported the letter was signed by 20 members of the bipartisan majority.
claims.verbatim: "We have heard from numerous citizens whose voting rights have been cancelled illegally and without just cause," the letter, signed by 20 members of the bipartisan majority, reads.
claims.notes: CONFLICTS WITH C12. Published 2026-07-29 under a 07-30 URL path. The earlier count may be signers at time of writing, but no page states that.

claims.claim: The legislators' letter says they have heard from numerous citizens whose voting rights have been cancelled illegally and without just cause.
claims.verbatim: We have heard from numerous citizens whose voting rights have been cancelled illegally and without just cause.
claims.notes: AN ALLEGATION, not an adjudicated finding. No statute page was reachable to test it. Always frame as 'the letter says' or 'legislators allege'. THE DECK MUST NOT SAY THE ACTION WAS ILLEGAL.

claims.claim: The legislators' letter says the division's actions threaten to deprive Alaskans of their most fundamental right in a democracy and that the mistakes should be addressed immediately.
claims.value: most fundamental right in a democracy
claims.verbatim: Your actions threaten to deprive Alaskans of their most fundamental right in a democracy, and correction of your department's mistakes should be addressed immediately.
claims.notes: Quoted identically by two independent newsrooms, which raises confidence in the letter's text even though the letter was unreachable. Still the legislators' characterization.

claims.claim: Rep. Ky Holland helped organize the letter and said there is not much time to correct the mistakes because the August 18 primary is just weeks away.
claims.verbatim: Holland was leery of Beecher's explanation for removing so many voters and said there's not much time to correct the mistakes because the Aug. 18 primary is just weeks away.
claims.notes: A reporter's paraphrase containing the date, not a direct quote. Attribute the urgency to Holland; take the date itself from C17, which is primary.

claims.claim: The State of Alaska Office of the Lieutenant Governor refers to the August 18 primary ballot in an official release.
claims.verbatim: The State of Alaska has opened an investigation into his declaration of candidacy for United States Senate before determining whether he may appear on the August 18 primary ballot.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Office of the Lieutenant Governor
claims.notes: PRIMARY SOURCE for the election date only. elections.alaska.gov returned 503 on every path, so the Lieutenant Governor's office, which oversees elections, is the closest reachable state source. The release itself concerns an unrelated candidacy matter.

claims.claim: A joint Division of Elections and DMV statement said Elections most recently asked DMV to compare lists in March 2026, which produced the letters.
claims.verbatim: "Elections has conducted this sort of list maintenance for years," the statement reads. "Elections most recently asked DMV to compare lists in March 2026, resulting in the 3,000 letters that Elections recently sent."
claims.notes: THE MECHANISM, in the agencies' own quoted words: one agency asked another to compare lists. This is the deck's 'not AI, a list comparison' anchor. Note the four-month gap between the March comparison and the July letters, which no source explains.

claims.claim: The joint Division of Elections and DMV statement said all the qualified voters who received these letters can still vote in the upcoming elections.
claims.verbatim: all the qualified voters who received these letters can still vote in the upcoming elections.
claims.notes: The state's defense. REQUIRED for fairness. Consistent with C09.

claims.claim: House Minority Leader DeLena Johnson said that if a voter's records indicate they are not a U.S. citizen, flagging that record for review is a reasonable and responsible step.
claims.verbatim: If a voter's records indicate they are not a U.S. citizen, flagging that record for review is a reasonable and responsible step.
claims.notes: This is the ONLY appearance of the word 'review' in the fetched reporting, and it is a legislator saying what SHOULD happen, not a description of what the division did. MUST NOT be presented as evidence that a human review step existed.

claims.claim: As of July 30 the Division of Elections had not answered specific questions about the legislators' letter, and a spokesman said the division would respond.
claims.verbatim: The Division of Elections did not answer specific questions about the legislators' letter but a spokesman said the division would respond.
claims.notes: ANCHORS THE DECK'S TENSE. Restoration status is undetermined as of 2026-08-01. The deck must say the division had said it would respond, never that it refused.

claims.claim: Jeannie McLeod, 75, of Anchorage said that when she became a citizen in 2024 she legally changed her first name from Emily to Jeannie, the name she has always used.
claims.verbatim: Jeannie McLeod, 75, of Anchorage said when she became a citizen in 2024, she took the opportunity to legally change her first name from Emily to the one she's always used, Jeannie.
claims.notes: The named human case. The source does NOT state that the name change caused the flag, so the deck must not assert causation. Present the name change and the flag as what she reported, adjacent, never as cause and effect.

claims.claim: Jeannie McLeod said she was mailed a voter's card carrying her old name and asked why the state would take her off and reinstate her under a name that is not legally hers.
claims.value: a name that is not legally mine
claims.verbatim: Last Thursday, I was mailed a voter's card with the old name. Hello? Like, I was on the voters list as Jeannie McLeod. Why would they take it off and reinstate me with a name that is not legally mine?
claims.notes: Verbatim from a targeted showrunner re-fetch on 2026-08-01. Straight quotes only when set on a slide. Carries no em dash, unlike her second quote, which must therefore not be used verbatim under the house rule.

claims.claim: KMXT reported that some affected voters got their driver's licenses before they were citizens and registered to vote after becoming citizens.
claims.verbatim: Some voters obtained licenses before citizenship, then registered after becoming citizens.
claims.notes: THE FAILURE MODE, stated plainly: the two records are true at different times, and the comparison has no way to see the order. Retrieved as a structured extraction rather than as a quoted sentence, so treat the wording as the outlet's substance rather than as an exact quotation on a slide.

claims.claim: Rep. Ky Holland said the timing of the effort seemed designed to cause more confusion and to undermine trust in the voting rolls.
claims.value: undermine trust in our voting rolls
claims.verbatim: The timing of this effort by the Division of Elections seemed to be … quite frankly, it seemed to be designed in order to try and cause more confusion and to undermine trust in our voting rolls,
claims.notes: AN ALLEGATION ABOUT MOTIVE by a legislator who helped organize the letter. Contains an ellipsis. Use with caution or not at all; the concrete McLeod material is stronger and fairer than an imputed motive.

claims.claim: The Department of the Air Force is offering approximately 4,700 acres of underutilized land across Joint Base Elmendorf Richardson, Eielson Air Force Base and Clear Space Force Station.
claims.verbatim: The DAF is offering approximately 4,700 acres of underutilized land across Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Eielson Air Force Base, and Clear Space Force Station.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Department of the Air Force
claims.notes: PRIMARY SOURCE. BACKGROUND, dated 2026-04-10, outside the story window, and must be labeled as background on any slide that uses it. 'Approximately' is the Air Force's own hedge.

claims.claim: Twelve parcels have been identified for potential development under the Air Force enhanced use lease model.
claims.verbatim: Twelve parcels have been identified for potential development.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Department of the Air Force
claims.notes: PRIMARY SOURCE. BACKGROUND. The page states NO lease term in years; the widely reported '50 years' was checked and killed.

claims.claim: Candidate for governor Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins said he opposes the construction of data centers in Alaska until the Legislature can pass comprehensive regulation on data center development.
claims.value: no new data centers until regulation
claims.verbatim: Seeking to head off concerns about his funding from Outsiders who work for AI companies, Kreiss-Tomkins issued a statement Thursday noting that he opposes the construction of data centers in Alaska until the state Legislature "can pass comprehensive regulation on data center development."
claims.notes: The article does NOT use the word 'moratorium'. Do not put that word in his mouth. A candidate position, not policy.

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins said Alaska should have a process and a policy, does not have one now, and until it does nothing should happen.
claims.verbatim: I think very clearly we should have a process and a policy we don't right now, and so until we do, nothing should happen,
claims.notes: Useful as a governance beat because it is a named candidate asserting the absence of a process, rather than the deck asserting it. The deck itself CANNOT claim Alaska has no AI statute; that claim was checked and killed as unprovable from any reachable page.

killed.claim: Air Force enhanced use leases run up to 50 years
killed.why: Re-fetched af.mil twice; the page gives no term in years. Unsupported.

killed.claim: Chris Waigl, naturalized 2025, was among the affected voters
killed.why: The name appears on no fetched page. Scout error. Only Jeannie McLeod is named.

killed.claim: Alaska has no AI-specific statute on the books
killed.why: A negative cannot be asserted from pages that returned 403. akleg.gov 403, NCSL tracker unreachable. UNUSABLE.

killed.claim: SB 250 passed the Senate 2026-05-16 and died in House Community and Regional Affairs
killed.why: akleg.gov 403, legiscan 403, openstates served an empty shell. Zero fetched evidence.

killed.claim: There was no human verification step between the DMV flag and the inactive status
killed.why: No fetched page states this either way. The honest form is that no published account describes one.

killed.claim: Two further Beecher quotes surfaced in a first-pass summary
killed.why: Did not reproduce on targeted verbatim re-fetch. Killed under the named-quote rule.

killed.claim: AS 15.07 requires specified steps before a registration is made inactive
killed.why: akleg.gov 403, justia 403, touchngo 503. The illegality allegation stands untested against statutory text.

killed.claim: The July 22 hearing was before a named committee
The Division of Elections has restored some or all of the 3,048
killed.why: No evidence either way. Undetermined as of 2026-08-01.

open_questions: RESTORATION STATUS UNDETERMINED AS OF 2026-08-01. elections.alaska.gov returned HTTP 503 on the homepage and two subpaths. The last fetchable statement is C21. The deck's tense must be 'as of August 1 the division had not publicly reversed the action and had said it would respond', never 'the division refused'.

HUMAN REVIEW. No fetched source describes a human verification step between the flag and the status change, in either direction. Correct slide phrasing is 'no published account describes a human verification step', with absence of description acknowledged as not being evidence of absence.
SIGNER COUNT. 23 (Alaska Public Media / KMXT, 07-30) vs 20 members of the bipartisan majority (Alaska's News Source, 07-29). The letter was unreachable. Report the range or attribute the number.

3,500 VS 3,048 ARE DIFFERENT QUANTITIES. 3,500 is approximately letters sent; 3,048 is the number moved to inactive. The Alaska Public Media headline as fetched reads '3,000' while its URL slug says 3-500, suggesting a post-publication revision.
TIMING GAP. The comparison was requested in March 2026; the letters went out in July, weeks before the primary. No source explains the four-month gap. Holland's timing complaint is an allegation.
STATUTORY BASIS UNTESTED. No statute page loaded, so the deck cannot evaluate the illegality claim and must frame it strictly as an allegation.
sourcing_assessment: The core is solid. The two load-bearing numbers, 3,048 and the roughly 200 normal quarterly yield, are each confirmed verbatim; 3,048 is attributed to a division spokesman and repeated by the same newsroom a week later; the Beecher 'probably very old data' quote reproduced exactly on targeted re-fetch; and the mechanism is documented in the agencies' own quoted words as one agency asking another to compare lists, which is exactly what the deck's thesis needs. Two independent newsrooms quote the legislators' letter identically. The thin layers are primary sourcing and law: elections.alaska.gov returned 503 on every path, akleg.gov returned 403, and all three statute hosts failed, so the Division's own statement, the hearing record, the letter itself and the text of AS 15.07 were all unreachable. The two primary sources landed (the Lieutenant Governor's newsroom for the election date, the Air Force release for the acreage) satisfy the gate but neither is the central document. Practical consequence: the deck cannot say the action was illegal, cannot say no human reviewed the flags, cannot use SB 250 or the no-AI-statute claim, and must state restoration status as undetermined as of 2026-08-01.
